title: Sinus lift
what: The surgeon adds bone graft material to your upper jaw, under the sinus. This gives enough bone to hold an implant.
why: When there is not enough bone in the upper back jaw to place an implant.
duration: surgery usually takes 30 to 90 minutes; the bone usually takes several months to heal
tell_doctor: Chronic runny nose, sinusitis, or a deviated septum
Blood thinners. Your doctor will say what to stop and when
Diabetes, heart disease, osteoporosis, and medicines for it
Allergies, especially to antibiotics and painkillers

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: You usually need a CT scan of your jaw, sometimes an ENT check and blood tests.

prepare.title: Treatment first
prepare.text: Bad teeth, gums, and a runny nose are treated before surgery.

prepare.title: Smoking
prepare.text: Try not to smoke before and after surgery. Bone heals worse in smokers.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Eat beforehand if you have local anesthesia. With sedation, the clinic will tell you when to stop eating.

bring: Someone to take you home, if you have sedation
steps: The doctor checks your scans again and goes over the plan
You get numbing, sometimes with sedation
The surgeon gently lifts the floor of the sinus
Bone graft material is placed underneath
Sometimes the implant is placed right away
feel: During surgery: pressure and vibration, but no pain
Afterward: a swollen cheek, sometimes a bruise, for a few days
A little blood from the nose in the first days
after: Hold something cold to your cheek on the first day
For two weeks, do not blow your nose hard. Sneeze with your mouth open
No flying, diving, or saunas until your doctor says it is OK
Take the medicines your doctor prescribed
Stitches usually come out after 7 to 14 days
red_flags: A fever over 38°C (100.4°F), growing swelling, or pus
Heavy bleeding from the mouth or nose that will not stop: call emergency services
Grains of material coming out of your nose, or liquid from your nose when you drink

faq.q: When can the implant go in?
faq.a: Sometimes right away. If there is little bone, usually after a few months, once it has healed.
Usually moderate pain for the first days. The painkillers your doctor prescribes will help.

reminders.text: Sinus lift tomorrow. Bring your scans and medicine list, and do not smoke. Eat only as the clinic told you.
